feed.title: Hardware, CAD & Embedded — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: 5Vpld
entry.summary: A collection of scripts and tools for the few still-made 5V programmable logic parts (Atmel ATF150x, GAL). Unlike modern FPGA toolchains it focuses on legacy 5V logic: the practical way to program these rare parts in retro and repair projects.

entry.title: Flipper Zero Tutorials
entry.summary: A large tutorial repository for the Flipper Zero covering apps, hardware add-ons and usage. Unlike the official docs it goes into community projects: practical, video-backed guides that also cover accessories like SAO badges and the FlipBoard.

entry.title: ISA
entry.summary: The automation engineering society, awarding certificates against the IEC 62443 industrial cybersecurity standard. Unlike IT security bodies it addresses operational technology, where the priority is not confidentiality but continuity.

entry.title: Digi-Key
entry.summary: An electronics component distributor with a strong catalogue, datasheets and parametric search. Against other distributors it wins on stock depth and single-unit sales — buying one part for a prototype is unremarkable here.

entry.title: EveryCircuit
entry.summary: Circuit simulation with real-time animation, working on mobile as well. Against Falstad it offers a touch interface and lets you drag component values and watch the result change immediately.

entry.title: Falstad Circuit Simulator
entry.summary: A simulator that animates current flowing through a circuit you draw, with voltage and current shown in colour. Against SPICE it aims at intuition rather than numerical accuracy — it is for seeing how a circuit works.

entry.title: FPGA4Fun
entry.summary: Projects that introduce FPGAs through hardware description languages, each producing a working circuit. Unlike a university course it starts from the project — something that works before any theory.

entry.title: FreeCAD
entry.summary: A parametric 3D CAD modeller where you go back up the design tree and change a dimension. That parametric approach is the split from Blender: Blender sculpts polygons, this designs a manufacturable part.

entry.title: KiCad
entry.summary: An open-source suite covering the whole electronics design flow from schematic to PCB layout. Against Eagle and Altium there is no layer count or board size limit — no free-tier ceiling at all.

entry.title: Octopart
entry.summary: A search engine for electronic components that compares stock and price across distributors on one page. That is what saves you checking Digi-Key and Mouser separately — you see availability while still designing.

entry.title: Open Circuits
entry.summary: A book of high-resolution cross-sections of electronic components, showing the insides of resistors, capacitors and connectors. Against datasheets it shows how a component is made — the abstract symbol becomes a physical object.

entry.title: PC-Builds
entry.summary: PC building tools with a bottleneck calculator that estimates CPU-to-GPU balance per game and resolution. Where PCPartPicker answers compatibility, this answers whether the balance makes sense.

entry.title: PCPartPicker
entry.summary: Checks part compatibility and compares prices while you plan a PC build. Against a manual list it catches the mismatch in advance — an underpowered PSU or a cooler that will not clear the case.

entry.title: RTINGS
entry.summary: Reviews TVs, headphones, monitors and mice through laboratory measurements, with methodology and raw data published. Unlike opinion reviews the results are measurable, and you can reweight the score for your own use.

entry.title: TechSpecs
entry.summary: A search engine for the specifications of consumer electronics, with comparison. Against manufacturer pages the data is normalised, so the same property written under two different names by two brands lines up.

entry.title: Thingiverse
entry.summary: The community archive of 3D printing models, mostly Creative Commons licensed and shared with print settings. Against Printables and MakerWorld it is the oldest and largest — still the first place to look for a niche part.

entry.title: Wokwi
entry.summary: Simulates Arduino, ESP32 and STM32 in the browser, with virtual sensors and displays attached. Against real hardware you start without waiting for a board — the logic gets verified before anything is soldered.

entry.title: Onshape
entry.summary: Parametric CAD entirely in the browser, working on a database rather than files, so branching and merging behave like Git — something SolidWorks does not offer.

entry.title: McMaster-Carr
entry.summary: An industrial parts catalogue where nearly every item has a downloadable CAD model, which turns it into a reference whenever a design needs a real bolt’s dimensions.

entry.title: Eclipse Ditto
entry.summary: Keeps device state server-side as a digital twin, so the last known state stays queryable and commands queue up even while the device sleeps.

entry.title: SmartVision
entry.summary: Video surveillance software with a Turkish interface covering camera management and recording — a practical option locally for language and support reasons.

entry.title: Anyka Kamera Firmware
entry.summary: Custom firmware for Anyka-based cameras, covering a family OpenIPC does not. Most cheap Chinese cameras use this chipset.

entry.title: AK3918 Kamera Notları
entry.summary: A thread accumulating hardware notes and firmware dumps for one camera SoC. For models like this, a single issue thread is usually the only source there is.

entry.title: OpenIPC
entry.summary: Open firmware for IP cameras that removes the vendor cloud and exposes the RTSP stream directly on your own network — the way to run a camera without putting it on the internet.

entry.title: OpenIPC Firmware
entry.summary: The supported chipset list and build instructions — check whether your camera’s SoC is on it before you buy.

entry.title: OpenIPC Coupler
entry.summary: Moves between camera firmwares and back to stock — often the only recovery tool you have while experimenting.

entry.title: OpenIPC Kurulum
entry.summary: The flashing steps and, more importantly, the way back. Attempting this without a serial console raises the bricking risk considerably.

entry.title: Advantech Edge AI SDK
entry.summary: A development kit for running models on industrial edge hardware — where certified equipment is required, a Raspberry Pi-class board does not qualify.

entry.title: Allwinner V821
entry.summary: A technical summary of the V821 SoC including its image pipeline and NPU capability — a comparison point when choosing silicon for a camera or edge AI project.

entry.title: AvaotaF1 İncelemesi
entry.summary: An article summarising the board’s specifications and likely uses — a quick look before diving into the repo.

entry.title: AvaotaF1
entry.summary: A coin-sized RISC-V Linux board with 64 MB RAM, MIPI camera, SPI display and Wi-Fi. Running full Linux rather than a microcontroller at that scale is what makes it unusual.

entry.title: LiteEMF
entry.summary: Embedded libraries and firmware repositories weighted towards USB HID and wireless input devices — a reference for controller and keyboard protocols.

entry.title: Kontrol Sistemleri Uygulamada
entry.summary: The engineering-intuition side of the same theory: how you actually tune a PID, what noise and saturation do to it. The half that belongs alongside the lecture course.

entry.title: Kontrol Sistemleri Dersleri
entry.summary: A full lecture series on control theory — transfer functions, stability criteria, state space — building the mathematics in academic order.

entry.title: CadXStudio
entry.summary: A browser tool generating CAD models from text, reaching into CAM as well. Aimed at simple parts without drafting skill, not at precision engineering.

entry.title: ORCAS
entry.summary: A remote-controlled airsoft turret where embedded control, video streaming and mechanical design meet in one project — showing the integration problems finished products hide.

entry.title: Taret Süspansiyon Günlüğü
entry.summary: A build diary for a homemade turret with the failed attempts left in — what a real design process looks like, unlike a polished tutorial.

entry.title: GrabCAD · Mini Tank
entry.summary: A shared tracked robot platform model — a way to start from a working design instead of drawing chassis geometry from scratch.
